_how: Recipe for shorts.build (video-machine). 13 clips from Kate Carney's (Church Onsite Wastewater Consultants) guest episode, take 160319 (Zoom HD 1280x720, speaker view, no upscale; source = the clean remix with Ashley's room echo reduced, in sync). keep = inclusive word-index ranges; fillers skip automatically; max_gap 1.0. Posting plan: release week 2026-12-16..12-22, every clip to YouTube + TikTok, two a day at noon and 5 PM CT through 12-21, then one at noon 12-22; the five strongest (call-before-you-dig, chisel-a-mountain, short-term-rental, hundred-cheaper, high-road) also to Instagram and Facebook at noon on weekdays. {kate} tags Kate Carney, {church} Church Onsite Wastewater Consultants (cowastewater.com, no social links on its site; cowc.info did not load), {nowra} NOWRA (nowra.org links only Facebook facebook.com/NOWRAOnsite, plus X and LinkedIn), {cpow} CPOW (cpow.net links only Facebook facebook.com/ColoradoProfessionalsinOnsiteWastewater). No org has an Instagram, TikTok or YouTube account linked from its own site. The two Facebook pages need their numeric ids (Page transparency or view-source userID) before they tag; until then Facebook prints the plain name. The full episode ({episode}) is linked everywhere but Facebook.

clips.title:
Call the septic engineer
*before* you dig

youtube.title: Septic installers: call the engineer before you dig, not after

captions.facebook:
Picture an engineer pulling up to a job site where nothing matches the design she drew. {kate} of {church}, incoming vice president of {nowra} and active in {cpow}, says there's nothing worse, and it's why she tells every installer the same thing: call me ahead of time with any question you have. She would much rather field those calls than find out someone did whatever they thought was right. Repairs turn up things nobody planned for, and if you call for an inspection and she can't get there for a couple of days, she knows the machine sitting on site is costing you money. Her rule is simple: ask for permission, not forgiveness.

#septic #septicinstaller

clips.title:
My master's thesis was on
*water fleas*

youtube.title: From water fleas to septic design: how an aquatic biologist became an onsite engineer

captions.facebook:
Not many septic careers start with water fleas. {kate} of {church}, incoming vice president of {nowra} and active in {cpow}, did her master's thesis on them, then took a job as an aquatic biologist sampling streams and doing ecological assessments. She loved being in the field, but when winter hit, she says, you just had to analyze spreadsheets and write reports. She wasn't very happy at her firm, and that's what pushed her toward a very different kind of work. I loved hearing how she got here.

#septic

clips.title:
They chiseled part of a mountain
to fit one *drain field*

youtube.title: A septic drain field under a mountain parking lot: the hardest job Kate Carney designed

captions.facebook:
Here's a septic job you don't see every day. {kate} of {church}, incoming vice president of {nowra} and active in {cpow}, designed a system for a building on a mountainside, with a river on one side and the mountain going straight up on the other. The drain field ended up under the parking area above, built to hold fire trucks, and there still wasn't enough room, so the crew actually chiseled away part of the mountain. The other option was building a road up the mountain and pumping it farther up. It was very expensive, and she says she was lucky to have great excavators to pull it off.

#septic #drainfield

youtube.title: How a septic engineer picks a system: simplest first, then sand filters

captions.facebook:
Ever wonder how an engineer decides which septic system a property gets? {kate} of {church}, incoming vice president of {nowra} and active in {cpow}, says she goes from the simplest to the more complicated. If there's space and good soil, it's a simple gravity flow system. But density keeps growing in Colorado, and she runs into poor clay soils, small lots in the mountains and rock soil. Those conditions push her toward a sand filter or sometimes higher level treatment. It all comes down to the site and the soil.

#septic #septicdesign

clips.title:
Tell your septic designer if
it'll be a *rental*

youtube.title: Septic design: why owners must tell the engineer about short-term rental use

captions.facebook:
Here's what can happen when you leave out one detail. {kate} of {church}, incoming vice president of {nowra} and active in {cpow}, designed a house as a residential system, and right after it was installed, the owner went in for a short-term rental permit. He never told her that was the plan. In Colorado, after three bedrooms you only design for one person per bedroom, so the system couldn't handle a rental with more people. Now he's looking at adding on to a brand new system that just got put in the ground.

#septic #septicdesign

clips.title:
Reach the septic filter without
lying on your *belly*

youtube.title: Septic riser design: handles within 6 inches of the lid so nobody lies on their belly

captions.facebook:
Ask anyone who services septic tanks what they hate, and reaching way down into a tank is near the top of the list. {kate} of {church}, incoming vice president of {nowra} and active in {cpow}, designs around it. Every handle, effluent filter and float tree gets extended up to within six inches of the riser lid, so you can reach your hand in without laying on your belly. The cords are wrapped neatly and attached to the side, and the floats go on a separate float tree you can pull out and test.

#septic #septicmaintenance

youtube.title: A few boxes on a piece of paper is not a septic design

captions.facebook:
An excavator told {kate} of {church}, incoming vice president of {nowra} and active in {cpow}, that the other engineers he works with don't care where he puts the system, as long as it's within 50 feet of the test holes. Her reaction: that's not really a design. She says that's making the installer do the design. She sees plans that are a few boxes on a piece of paper with a tank size and rough dimensions. Hers show installers exactly what she wants, and she thinks that's why they have such a great relationship.

#septic #septicinstaller

clips.title:
My degrees never taught me
about *septic* systems

youtube.title: Why a small septic company should join its state association

captions.facebook:
When {kate} of {church}, incoming vice president of {nowra} and active in {cpow}, got into the industry, everything was on-the-job training. Her undergrad and graduate degrees never taught her about onsite wastewater. Now there are courses for soils, for design, for inspectors. She told me about teaching an inspector class where a man who had just bought a pump truck was so excited he wanted to take as many classes as he could. She loves that.

#septic

clips.title:
Septic problems get caught
at the *sale*

youtube.title: Septic inspections at property sale catch failing systems before the buyer moves in

captions.facebook:
You put a good chunk of your money into a down payment on a new house. A couple of days after you move in, there's sewage on the ground. {kate} of {church}, incoming vice president of {nowra} and active in {cpow}, says that's why the property sale is the time to find these problems: the money is there during that transaction to get it fixed. In Colorado, counties that adopted title transfer inspections are catching a lot of systems in need of repair, and some realtors tell clients to get one even where it's not required.

#septic #septicinspection

clips.title:
Don't aim yard drainage
at your *septic* system

youtube.title: Septic failures: irrigation and yard drainage pointed at the system

captions.facebook:
Not everyone who moves onto a septic system knows how it works. {kate} of {church}, incoming vice president of {nowra} and active in {cpow}, says some owners just irrigate their yard, not realizing the system is already trying to get water into the ground. She has also seen a few surface drainage problems where the septic designer and the person doing the grading and drainage never talked, so drainage ended up directed toward the system.

#septic

youtube.title: Hire the cheapest septic installer and you may pay for a second inspection

captions.facebook:
Picture a homeowner who found an installer who was a hundred dollars cheaper. {kate} of {church}, incoming vice president of {nowra} and active in {cpow}, goes out to inspect and finds several things that need to be corrected. That means she has to charge for another inspection, the process gets delayed, and the county has to come back out. Some owners even decide to move out of the house while they wait. She says that's why it's better for everyone when installers know what's expected: jobs go quicker and things go way smoother.

#septic #septicinstaller

clips.title:
We bought in right
before the *recession*

youtube.title: Septic design firm owner on buying a business right before the 2007 housing crash

captions.facebook:
The hardest stretch {kate} of {church}, incoming vice president of {nowra} and active in {cpow}, has been through as a business owner came right when she bought her business in 2007. The housing market declined, and since they did a lot of residential work, there were times they weren't getting paychecks. Builders were going out of business and even larger engineering firms were laying off people. She says it taught her to be grateful when there's too much work, and to know there will be ebbs and flows and to prepare for them.

#septic #smallbusiness

clips.title:
You can never go wrong
taking the *high road*

youtube.title: Septic business advice: you can never go wrong taking the high road

captions.facebook:
Getting undercut by a competitor stings. {kate} of {church}, incoming vice president of {nowra} and active in {cpow}, told me about a mentor of hers, an engineer and distributor, who said something that stuck with her: you can never go wrong taking the high road. If her price is higher because she's providing the product you actually need and not doing unethical things, so be it. And in the end, she says, it works out for her. I got chills when she said it.

#septic #septicbusiness
